arxiv-2101-01526.title: Harmonic ECME Excited by Energetic Electrons Travelling Inside A Coronal Loop
arxiv-2101-01526.creator: Mehdi Yousefzadeh, Hao Ning, Yao Chen
arxiv-2101-01526.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mehdi Yousefzadeh, Hao Ning, Yao Chen. A complete understanding of solar radio bursts requires developing numerical techniques which can connect large-scale activities with kinetic plasma processes. As a starting point, this study presents a numerical scheme combining three different techniques: (1) extrapolation of magnetic field overlying a specific active region in order to derive the background field, (2) guiding-center simulation of dynamics of millions of particles within a selected loop to reveal the integral velocity distribution function (VDF) around certain sections of the loop,

arxiv-2212-09895.title: Improved Long-Form Spoken Language Translation with Large Language Models
arxiv-2212-09895.creator: Arya D. McCarthy, Hao Zhang, Shankar Kumar, Felix Stahlberg, Axel H. Ng
arxiv-2212-09895.description: Abstract A challenge in spoken language translation is that plenty of spoken content is long-form, but short units are necessary for obtaining high-quality translations. To address this mismatch, we fine-tune a general-purpose, large language model to split long ASR transcripts into segments that can be independently translated so as to maximize the overall translation quality.

arxiv-2301-06194.title: Geometric Graph Learning with Extended Atom–Types Features for Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction
arxiv-2301-06194.creator: Md Masud Rana, Duc Duy Nguyen
arxiv-2301-06194.description: Abstract Understanding and accurately predicting protein-ligand binding affinity are essential in the drug design and discovery process. At present, machine learning-based methodologies are gaining popularity as a means of predicting binding affinity due to their efficiency and accuracy, as well as the increasing availability of structural and binding affinity data for protein-ligand complexes.

arxiv-2405-15719.title: Hierarchical Uncertainty Exploration via Feedforward Posterior Trees
arxiv-2405-15719.creator: Elias Nehme, Rotem Mulayoff, Tomer Michaeli
arxiv-2405-15719.description: Abstract When solving ill-posed inverse problems, one often desires to explore the space of potential solutions rather than be presented with a single plausible reconstruction. Valuable insights into these feasible solutions and their associated probabilities are embedded in the posterior distribution.

arxiv-2410-17355.title: All Entities are Not Created Equal: Examining the Long Tail for Fine-Grained Entity Typing
arxiv-2410-17355.creator: Advait Deshmukh Ashwin Umadi Dananjay Srinivas Maria Leonor Pacheco University of Colorado Boulder {advait.deshmukh, ashwin.umadi, dananjay.srinivas}@colorado.edu
arxiv-2410-17355.description: Abstract Pre-trained language models (PLMs) are trained on large amounts of data, which helps capture world knowledge alongside linguistic competence. Due to this, they are extensively used for ultra-fine entity typing tasks, where they provide the entity knowledge held in its parameter space.

arxiv-2503-11411.title: Empowering Time Series Analysis with Synthetic Data: A Survey and Outlook in the Era of Foundation Models Thanks: Junnan Li and Chenghao Liu are corresponding authors.
arxiv-2503-11411.creator: Xu Liu, Taha Aksu, Juncheng Liu, Qingsong Wen, Yuxuan Liang, Caiming Xiong, Silvio Savarese, Doyen Sahoo, Junnan Li, Chenghao Liu
arxiv-2503-11411.description: Abstract . Time series analysis is crucial for understanding dynamics of complex systems. Recent advances in foundation models have led to task-agnostic Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) and Large Language Model-based Time Series Models (TSLLMs), enabling generalized learning and integrating contextual information.

arxiv-2507-14593.title: Coordinate Heart System: A Geometric Framework for Emotion Representation
arxiv-2507-14593.creator: Omar Aldesi
arxiv-2507-14593.description: Abstract This paper presents the Coordinate Heart System (CHS), a geometric framework for emotion representation in artificial intelligence applications. We position eight core emotions as coordinates on a unit circle, enabling mathematical computation of complex emotional states through coordinate mixing and vector operations.

arxiv-2509-11758.title: Investigating the correlations of bulk properties of hyperon star with dark matter
arxiv-2509-11758.creator: Rashmita Jena, Padmalaya Dash, S.K. Biswal
arxiv-2509-11758.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rashmita Jena, Padmalaya Dash, S.K. Biswal. The strong gravitational pull of the neutron star leads to the accretion of dark matter (DM) inside the core of the neutron star. The accretion of DM affects the bulk properties of the neutron star. Here, we study how the accretion of WIMP (Weakly Interacting Massive Particles) dark matter particles affects the Δ − \Delta- admixed hyperon star’s bulk properties specifically mass, radius, tidal deformability, f − f- mode frequency and moment of inertia.

pmc-10641177.title: Spark plasma welding joining of copper- AISI4140 steel: Microstructures and mechanical properties
pmc-10641177.creator: Mehdi Naderi, Mohammad Reza Toroghinejad, Ahmad Kermanpur
pmc-10641177.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The main aim of this research study was to characterize the microstructures and mechanical properties of Cu-AISI4140 steel solid-state joining created via the spark plasma welding (SPW) method with and without using molds. To explore the effect of mold on the joining of copper/steel, the SPW process was done at 650 °C for 30 min under the pressure of 20 MPa, with and without mold.

pmc-10739021.title: PSYCHOMETRIC PROPERTIES OF THE KOREAN VERSION HOSPITAL SURVEY ON PATIENT SAFETY CULTURE IN HOME HEALTHCARE
pmc-10739021.creator: Kayoung Lee, Soohee Lee, Seoyoon Woo
pmc-10739021.description: Patient safety culture is essential for quality care in healthcare organizations. Instruments for patient safety have been developed and widely implemented in hospital settings. The revised hospital survey on patient safety culture (HSOPSC) is one of the representative instruments for evaluating patient safety culture. In 2021, the Korean version of the HSOPSC 2.0 (K-HSOPSC 2.0) was developed.

pmc-11607202.title: Recent advances on biogenesis, functions and therapeutic potential of long noncoding RNAs in T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
pmc-11607202.creator: Parminder Kaur, Pankaj Sharma, Prateek Bhatia, Minu Singh
pmc-11607202.description: T-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (T-ALL) is a highly aggressive form of ALL with at least 25% relapse rates. The high relapse rates are often linked to poor prognoses. More detailed studies for novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of T-ALL are required as the genetic and transcriptomic data currently available on T-ALL pathophysiology is insufficient.

pmc-12596996.title: Assessment of maternal-offspring selenium transfer in ewes and newborn lambs via serum, whole blood, and wool matrices
pmc-12596996.creator: Mehmet Çalışkan
pmc-12596996.description: Highlights•Selenium concentrations in whole blood, serum, and wool were analyzed for intra-individual consistency and for pairwise correlations between each ewe and her lamb.•Whole blood and serum selenium levels showed significant intra-group correlations in both ewes and lambs.•A significant maternal–offspring correlation was detected in whole blood selenium concentrations, but not in serum or wool.

pmc-12608482.title: A Spatial Point Feature-Based Registration Method for Remote Sensing Images with Large Regional Variations
pmc-12608482.creator: Yalun Zhao, Derong Chen, Jiulu Gong, Hui-liang Shen, Eryun Liu, Siyuan Cao
pmc-12608482.description: The accurate registration of image pairs is an indispensable key step in the process of disaster assessment, environmental monitoring, and change detection. However, obtaining correct matches from input images is difficult, especially from images with significant resolution and regional variations. The current image-registration algorithms perform poorly in this application scenario.

pmc-13210987.title: Exercise-Based Strategies from Warm-Up to Training: A Systematic Review of Performance Enhancement and Injury Prevention
pmc-13210987.creator: Wiktor Kłobuchowski, Maciej Skorulski, Kajetan Ornowski, Robert Roczniok, Adam Maszczyk, Bianca Callegari, Givago Silva Souza, Przemysław Pietraszewski, Szymon Kuliś
pmc-13210987.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Targeted training interventions, including neuromuscular warm-up protocols, eccentric resistance training, and dynamic stretching exercises, with limited and heterogeneous evidence on recovery strategies, have shown potential benefits for muscle performance and reductions in injury risk. Objective: To synthesize and structure contemporary evidence on exercise-based interventions spanning the pre-activity warm-up through post-activity recovery, emphasizing performance outcomes, injury-related effects, reported dose–response patterns, and implementation characteristics.
